message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that would take several years to complete. Here’s why:

| Factor | Why it matters | Rough estimate |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| **Height & Surface Area** | The tower is ~330 m tall and has a complex lattice structure. Even if you could paint a few hundred square meters per day, the total surface area is on the order of 10,000–15,000 m². | 10–15 k m² |
| **Safety & Logistics** | Workers need to be suspended on cables or use climbing rigs, and the tower is a UNESCO World Heritage site with strict regulations. | 1–2 years of planning + 1–2 years of actual work |
| **Weather & Scheduling** | Paint can only be applied under certain temperature and humidity conditions. The tower is open to the public, so work must be scheduled around tourist hours. | 2–3 years of intermittent work |
| **Regulatory Approvals** | Any major renovation requires approval from French heritage authorities and coordination with the Paris city council. | 6–12 months of approvals |

**Bottom line:** A full repaint of the Eiffel Tower would likely take **2–3 years** of intermittent work, plus additional time for planning, approvals, and logistics. This is a rough estimate; the exact duration would depend on the chosen paint system, crew size, and regulatory constraints.
